title: Photoreceptor Spectral Sensitivity in the Bumblebee, Bombus impatiens (Hymenoptera: Apidae)
why: Intracellular recordings in B. impatiens itself: UV, blue and green classes with peaks near 347, 424 and 539 nm, which is the species-level measurement for the Ultraviolet row of the common eastern bumblebee.

title: Photoreceptor processing speed and input resistance changes during light adaptation correlate with spectral class in the bumblebee, Bombus impatiens
why: Light-adapted integration time of B. impatiens photoreceptors (about 11 ms green, 16 ms UV, 19 ms blue), a species-level measure of how fast a bumblebee eye responds; gives a Speed row value for this species.

title: Differences in Photoreceptor Processing Speed for Chromatic and Achromatic Vision in the Bumblebee, Bombus terrestris
why: Genus-level comparator for Bombus speed (impulse response half-widths 7.9 ms green, 9.8 ms blue, 12.3 ms UV); B. impatiens is slower, so this sets the range inside the genus.

title: Spatial acuity of honeybee vision and its spectral properties
why: Behavioural grating acuity of the honeybee (about 0.34 cycles per degree), measured in Apis mellifera's own foragers; gives the Sharpness figure for the most photographed bee and shows acuity rests on the green channel.

title: Photoreceptor spectral sensitivities of the Small White butterfly Pieris rapae crucivora interpreted with optical modeling
why: Four visual pigments and eight photoreceptor classes in Pieris rapae crucivora, so how many colour classes the cabbage white has and where its UV and violet receptors sit.

title: The photoreceptor localization confirms the spectral heterogeneity of ommatidia in the male small white butterfly, Pieris rapae crucivora
why: Intracellular recordings of UV, blue, double-peaked blue and green receptors in the three ommatidial types of Pieris rapae; species-level support for the UV row and for the Colour row.

authors: Wang X-X, Liu Y-N, Huang C-Y, Li R-Y, Jiang Z-W, Liu C-Y, Liu T-X, Zhang Y
title: Light Intensity Modulates Locomotor Behavior and Predation in Different Color Morphs of the Harlequin Ladybird, Harmonia axyridis
why: Knockdown of two UV opsins and a long-wave opsin in Harmonia axyridis changes its movement, with blue and red light adding effects; evidence that the Asian lady beetle has UV and long-wave receptors that act on behaviour (not a spectral measurement).

title: Spectral properties of movement perception in the dronefly Eristalis
why: Motion neurons of Eristalis tenax peak near 350 nm (UV) and 475 nm for flashes and near 450 nm for moving gratings: a species-level spectral measurement for the drone fly's Ultraviolet row.

authors: Somanathan H, Kelber A, Borges RM, Wallen R, Warrant EJ
title: Visual ecology of Indian carpenter bees II: adaptations of eyes and ocelli to nocturnal and diurnal lifestyles
why: Facet size, rhabdom width, sensitivity and photoreceptor speed for three Xylocopa species; the within-genus comparator for the eastern carpenter bee's Sharpness and Speed rows (acuity travels within a genus).

authors: Egri A, Meszaros A, Kriska G, Fail J
title: Dichromacy in the brown marmorated stink bug? Spectral sensitivity of the compound eyes and phototaxis of Halyomorpha halys
why: Electroretinograms of Halyomorpha halys show green and UV receptors and no blue one; species-level measure for the Ultraviolet row.

authors: Crook DJ, Hull-Sanders HM, Hibbard EL, Mastro VC
title: A Comparison of Electrophysiologically Determined Spectral Responses in Six Subspecies of Lymantria
why: ERGs of the North American gypsy moth (L. dispar dispar) peak at 480-520 nm with a smaller UV peak at 340-380 nm and none in the red; fixes the Ultraviolet row for Lymantria dispar.

title: Eyeshine and spectral tuning of long wavelength-sensitive rhodopsins: no evidence for red-sensitive photoreceptors among five Nymphalini butterfly species
why: Long-wave pigment peaks (510-534 nm) measured in Nymphalis antiopa, Inachis (Aglais) io, Junonia coenia and Vanessa cardui, plus Pieris rapae for comparison; gives lambda max for four of the top-ranked butterflies.

title: Ultrastructure and adaptation in the retina of Aglais urticae (Lepidoptera)
why: Ommatidial structure of the small tortoiseshell's eye, with UV and blue sensitivity suggested for particular cells; the species' own retina anatomy for the Aglais genus.

authors: Gutierrez D, Rigosi E, Nagloo N, O'Carroll D, Warrant EJ
title: Spatial resolution and optical sensitivity in the compound eyes of two common European wasps, Vespula germanica and Vespula vulgaris
why: Interommatidial angles of 1.0 to 2.2 degrees and acceptance angles under 1.3 degrees in two social wasps; nearest measured relative (same family) for the paper wasp Polistes dominula's Sharpness row.
